newsitem.title: CHILE: CHILEAN SHARES SHED EARLY GAINS, CLOSE LOWER.
newsitem.headline: CHILEAN SHARES SHED EARLY GAINS, CLOSE LOWER.

text.p: Chilean stocks gave back early gains to close lower on the back of Wall Street's slide as local investors continued to digest company second-quarter earnings, said dealers.
The market is expected to hold steady at the opening with little news on the horizon to move individual stocks sharply, they said.
The 40-share index closed unofficially down 0.16 percent at 134.79 points. The general index shed 0.11 percent to 5,707.53 points.

Declining issues included Cristales, whose weeklong retreat began after the glass maker released disappointing earnings. There are also concerns that its television division was facing stiffer-than-expected competition, traders said.
"The company is finding it difficult to make its cable television business profitable," one trader said.
Cristales ended down 1.72 percent at 2,850 pesos.

Other decliners included the Chispa group of companies, which resumed their downward drift on sales by investors who bought the stock after May 30, making them ineligible to sell their shares to Spanish utility Endesa.
Endesa has said it will only buy stocks from investors owning them by the May 30 deadline.
Chispados ended down 2.6 percent at 185 pesos.
Gainers included brewery CCU, up 0.86 percent at 1,992 pesos, copper products maker Madeco, up 0.61 percent at 986 pesos, and pulp producer Copec, which rose 0.24 percent to 2,095 pesos.
